statement: There exists an isotropic log-concave probability law (X,Z) in R^2 for which ess sup_x C_P(law(Z|X=x))=infinity. Specifically take density exp(-(2+sqrt(2)x)) on x>=-sqrt(2), |z|<=x+sqrt(2). For x>-sqrt(2), Var(Z|X=x)=(x+sqrt(2))^2/3 and the conditional Poincare constant is at least this value.
assumptions: Poincare inequality uses the Euclidean derivative on the one-dimensional conditional support
Conditional law is the explicitly specified regular conditional distribution
Log-concavity includes convex supports with +infinity potential outside
proof_or_counterexample: Cone density (1/2)e^-s on s>=0, |y|<=s has S~Gamma(2,1), E S=2 and Var S=2. Y|S=s is uniform[-s,s], E Y^2=2, E Y=E SY=0. Affine normalization X=(S-2)/sqrt(2), Z=Y/sqrt(2) gives covariance I. Conditional variance is a^2/3 and g(z)=z has gradient energy 1. The event S>sqrt(6M) has probability (1+sqrt(6M))e^-sqrt(6M)>0 for all M>0.

statement: For the isotropic log-concave cone law in w359-C1 and f(x,z)=z^2, d/dx E[f(X,Z)|X=x]=2(x+sqrt(2))/3 while E[partial_x f(X,Z)|X=x]=0 for x>-sqrt(2). Therefore full isotropy and log-concavity do not justify differentiating a conditional mean as if its conditional law were independent of x.
assumptions: The same explicit cone law as w359-C1
Polynomial f=z^2, whose moments are finite under the law

source.quote: Its conditional mean is m(x)=a^2/3 and m'(x)=2a/3.

proof_or_counterexample: Integrate z^2 against the uniform[-a,a] conditional law to obtain a^2/3; a=x+sqrt(2), so differentiate directly. The partial derivative of z^2 with respect to x is identically zero.
